problem.statement: Reviews with release r1 got 13 of 40 development reviews wrong: type_changed×3, field_removed×4, field_renamed×3, required_added×2, enum_value_removed×1.

hypothesis: If the change-review skill also compares contract_before and contract_after field by field (recursing into nested objects and array items) and blocks consumer-breaking differences, then breaking changes that are currently approved will be sent back with the correct field named. That covers removed or renamed fields, type changes, newly required fields, removed enum values, unit or format changes and tightened constraints. Doc-only changes and added optional fields should still be approved. Measured result: development accuracy went from about 0.675 on the observed sample to 1.0 on the 60 dev cases, with 0 of 38 breaking changes approved and 0 of 22 safe changes blocked.
expected_benefit: Fewer approved breaking changes, with safe changes still approved.
possible_regressions: Each review runs one more step

The dev cases only contain type_changed, field_removed, field_renamed, required_added and enum_value_removed as breaking kinds, and doc-only, optional-field-added and no-contract-change as safe kinds. Every other rule (units, formats, constraints, nullability, required to optional, enum additions, composition keywords) is untested against labels.

When the label is ambiguous (making a field nullable or optional, adding an enum value), I chose to block when in doubt because the gate allows no extra escapes but some margin on false alarms. The held-out labelling convention may differ.

Field-path convention for nested and array fields: I use dot paths such as 'tolerance.lower' and leave out 'items' for arrays. If the held-out scorer expects 'items' or '[]' in the path, nested array findings may count as the wrong field.

change.summary: Added candidate/validators/interface_compat.mjs, a plain-JS check with no imports. It walks both schemas recursively and builds dot paths from the root, skipping 'items' for arrays. BLOCKING findings: a property removed (reported under the old path); a rename, detected when a removed field and an added field have the same schema once documentation is ignored, reported only under the old path; any change to the set of allowed types, including adding null or nullable:true; a new required field, or an optional field made required; a required field made optional; an enum value removed, an enum added to a field that had none, or a const changed; x-unit/unit, format or content encoding changed; a constraint tightened (min/max, length, item count, pattern, multipleOf, uniqueItems, additionalProperties:false); a non-documentation change to oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not/$ref or to a non-object items schema. ADVISORY only: an enum value added, a constraint loosened, an enum or const removed, a default changed, a unit annotation added or dropped. IGNORED: description, title, examples, $comment and key order. Ran `node check.mjs`: accuracy 1.0, breaking changes approved 0 of 38, safe changes blocked 0 of 22, no errors.
